abstract: Maintains indoor sound isolation and mechanical ventilation noise measurements
system_message:
You are the Acoustic and Environmental Engineer (ACO), responsible for maintaining indoor sound isolation, mechanical ventilation noise measurements, and arena reverberation baseline surveys across potential host arenas.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Arena Sound Reverberation（REVERB）
information_points.content:
ACO-REVERB-7MD：According to the electro-acoustic commission survey measuring the unoccupied main bowl volume, the Centennial Multi-Purpose Velodrome exhibits a mid-frequency reverberation decay time (T60 decay time at 500 Hz to 1000 Hz octave bands) of 1.2 s.
ACO-REVERB-1MK：According to the electro-acoustic commission survey of the unoccupied main bowl acoustic volume, the mid-frequency reverberation decay time (T60 decay time at 500 Hz to 1000 Hz octave bands) for the Metropolitan Exhibition Coliseum is 1.6 s.
ACO-REVERB-M9G：According to the electro-acoustic commission survey, the Riverside Congress and Athletics Arena has a mid-frequency reverberation decay time (T60 across the 500 Hz to 1000 Hz octave bands) of 2.0 s within its unoccupied main bowl volume.

information_points.title: Maintains indoor sound isolation and mechanical ventilation noise measurements（NOISE）
information_points.content:
ACO-NOISE-YYV：For the Centennial Multi-Purpose Velodrome, environmental acoustics baseline testing recorded a main bowl HVAC background noise rating of 38 dBA at ear height on the competition floor while ventilation operated at full cooling capacity.
ACO-NOISE-989：For the Riverside Congress and Athletics Arena, the main bowl HVAC background noise rating measured at ear height on the arena competition floor under full ventilation cooling capacity is 28 dBA as an A-weighted continuous equivalent sound pressure level.
ACO-NOISE-LZY：For the Metropolitan Exhibition Coliseum, the environmental acoustics baseline report indicates an A-weighted continuous equivalent sound pressure level showing a main bowl HVAC background noise rating of 33 dBA across the arena competition floor at ear height with ventilation running at full cooling capacity.
